units.source_text: 祖母的逝世，使我对自家的佛坛头一次产生了一种说不出的感情。

en.t: My grandmother's death made me feel, for the first time, an indescribable emotion toward the Buddhist altar in our home.

units.source_text: 我选择祖父看不见的时候，

en.t: I chose moments when my grandfather could not see me,

units.source_text: 从外面把关得严严实实的佛堂隔扇打开一道细缝，

en.t: and from the outside opened a narrow crack in the tightly shut sliding doors of the Buddhist room,
opening them and closing them, closing them and opening them again,

units.source_text: 不知疲倦地偷看供灯照亮的佛坛，消磨时光。

en.t: passing the time by tirelessly peeking at the altar lit by the offering lamp.

units.source_text: 但是，我记得我是不愿意敞开隔扇去靠近佛坛的。

en.t: But I remember that I was unwilling to slide the doors wide open and go near the altar.

units.source_text: 夕阳西沉，地平线上只有山和山巅染满了明亮亮的光辉，一派恬静的气氛。

en.t: The evening sun sank in the west, and on the horizon only the mountains and their peaks were dyed in bright light, filling everything with a peaceful air.

units.source_text: 我抬眼仰望，不知为什么，总联想到八岁时我所看见的佛坛上供灯的颜色。

en.t: When I raised my eyes and looked up, for some reason I always thought of the color of the offering lamp I had seen on the altar when I was eight.

units.source_text: 佛堂的白色隔扇上，胡乱地涂了一行长长的祖母的戒名，是用合乎我这个普通小学一年级学生身份的片假名书写的。

en.t: On the white sliding doors of the Buddhist room, a long line of my grandmother's posthumous Buddhist name had been scrawled messily in katakana, just as befitted an ordinary first grader like me.

units.source_text: 这些字，一直保留到出卖这栋房子的时候。

en.t: Those characters remained there until the house was sold.
